proposed.explanation:
TMGH shows strong fundamental momentum in FY2025. Gross profit grew approximately 49% year-over-year (from 14.00 billion to 20.86 billion EGP), and verified EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP, a gain of roughly 59%. Total equity expanded about 21% to 157.7 billion EGP, indicating the company is retaining and compounding capital. At the current price of 82.50 EGP, the trailing P/E is about 11.8×, which appears reasonable for a company delivering near-60% EPS growth. The net-profit-to-gross-profit ratio of roughly 87% (18.20 B / 20.86 B) suggests very low operating overhead relative to earnings, a sign of operational efficiency.

For an investor with a 10+ year horizon, high loss tolerance, and no near-term liquidity needs, initiating a position in a large, growing company at a single-digit-plus P/E is consistent with a long-term wealth-building strategy. I am capping the purchase at 606 shares (50,000 EGP) so that TMGH represents exactly 50% of the 100,000 EGP portfolio, respecting the diversification ceiling. The remaining 50,000 EGP in cash preserves flexibility to add to the position on weakness or diversify into other names later.

Key limitations and risks: (1) Only two fiscal years are available, so the growth trend cannot be confirmed as sustainable. (2) The 2024 net-profit figure is marked AMBIGUOUS (obscured by an auditor's stamp), so I could not independently verify the exact net-profit growth rate; I relied on the verified EPS figures instead. (3) No data on debt levels, free cash flow, dividend policy, sector competition, or the reason for the 2024 restatement was provided. (4) A single-year snapshot does not capture cyclicality. The investor should monitor subsequent filings and consider adding other holdings to reduce single-stock concentration over time.
unused_figures: Net profit FY2024 (Restated) = 12,769,517,325 EGP [TMGH-TMGH_FY2025_consolidated_en-p7-56] – marked AMBIGUOUS because digits are covered by an auditor's stamp. This prevents a direct year-over-year net-profit growth calculation; I substituted the verified EPS growth (4.38 → 6.98, ≈59%) as the growth indicator instead.
limitations: Only two fiscal years (2024 restated and 2025) are available; no longer trend or cyclicality can be assessed.
The 2024 net-profit figure is unreadable, so exact net-profit growth could not be confirmed.
No information on debt, free cash flow, dividends, sector dynamics, or the reason for the 2024 restatement.
A single-company position of 50% still carries significant idiosyncratic risk; the investor should seek to diversify in future periods.
